## Conflicts

| temp-id | parties | contradiction | proposed resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| CF-057 | WS-A1 §6.3 ("event store / run ledger ≈ OpenHands `EventLog`/conversation tree") vs WS-B1 §6.2 `fork` | OpenHands' `fork()` **copies** events into a new conversation; WS-B1 chooses fork-**by-reference** (`forked_from{run_id, at_seq, source_head_hash}`) with copy only at bundle export | Not a real contradiction: WS-A1's "≈" is a positioning analogy. Record ADR-0027 as the contract; WS-A1's line stays as history. WS-I3 materializes lineage on export. |
| CF-058 | WS-L1 §6.5 invariant I4 ("events crossing the boundary are byte-identical to events in the ledger") vs ADR-0029 | Wire and stored encodings may legitimately differ (compression at rest, generated bindings); requiring byte-identical *stored* bytes would force one encoding on both sides | Reword I4 to "byte-identical **canonical form** (hash-equal) on both sides of the boundary"; the WS-H6 chain is over the canonical form, so tamper evidence is preserved. |
| CF-059 | Ontology v0.1 `observability level` = `{events, model_io, end_state, ledger}` "stamped on every ledger event (WS-B1)" vs WS-B1 §6.3 | `ledger` ("full IR-native typed ledger") is a property of the *participant class* (native ⇒ ledger), not something an individual event can carry independently of `events`; stamping it per event is redundant and lets a hosted row claim `ledger` | WS-A2 to settle: keep the four-valued set for `MetricDeclaration.requires_observability` (T-LCD-15) but define `ledger` as *derived* (`participant_class = native`), so the per-event stamp is `{events, model_io, end_state}` ∪ derived `ledger`. If WS-A2 keeps it stamped, B1 adds a validation rule `ledger ⇒ native`. |
| CF-060 | WS-B1 §6.3 structural ids `run_id ⊃ turn_id ⊃ model_call_id ⊃ tool_call_id` vs WS-B2 §6.4 `run_id ⊃ turn_id ⊃ step_id ⊃ call_id` | Same chain, two spellings; WS-B2 also derives `effect_id` from the pair | Coordination, not contradiction (mirror of CF-064). Synthesis picks one spelling and records it in the ontology; B1 recommends `model_call_id`/`tool_call_id` (unambiguous; "step" and "call" collide with model calls) and accepts WS-B2's `effect_id` derivation unchanged. |

Accepted by WS-B1 without contradiction: CF-036 (IR owns the `Observation` payload type, B1 owns the envelope), CF-064 (WS-B2's effect event names adopted verbatim as `action.effect.*`).

## Ontology terms

| term | definition | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **run ledger** | The authoritative record of one run: the typed append-only event log + the content-addressed blob store it references + the immutable run manifest (payload of `lifecycle.run.created`). Native and typed; never interchange-shaped. | WS-B1 / ADR-0026. Canonical noun for "event store" in doc 3 §2.2. |
| **ledger event** | One typed, immutable record in the run ledger: envelope + class-specific payload; identified by `(run_id, event_id)`, ordered by `(run_id, seq)`, hashed into the run's chain. | WS-B1 |
| **event envelope** | The class-independent fields of every ledger event: `event_id, run_id, seq, ts, plane, class, schema_version, producer, participant_class, observability_level, durability, scope{turn_id, model_call_id, tool_call_id, effect_id, child_run_id}, lease_generation, parent_event_id, causes[], refs[], ir_refs[], provenance, prev_hash, hash`. | WS-B1 §6.3 |
| **event class** | A named event type `plane.noun.verb` with a versioned payload schema, a declared `durability`, the minimum `observability_level` at which it is expected, and a declared lowering to the Hosting-ABI vocabulary or `none`. Each event *family* has exactly one home plane (WS-A2). | WS-B1; families listed in dossier §6.3 |
| **materialized view** | A derived, rebuildable projection of a durable ledger prefix (context view, run summary, HEAD, index, effect ledger, audit chain head, results row, cost totals) stamped with the `(run_id, seq)` watermark and view-policy version it was derived from (`derived_from`); never written except by projection; two rebuilds yield equal `view_hash`. | WS-B1 / ADR-0026; consumers D1, B2, H6, J5, L2 |
| **authoritative record** | The parts of a run's state that are not derived from anything else: log + blobs + manifest. Everything not in it is a materialized view or excluded from the ledger by the persistence policy. | ADR-0026 |
| **persistence policy** | The single declared table stating, per event class, `durability ∈ {ledger, ephemeral}` and the offload threshold; never encoded ad hoc in producers. | Codex `rollout/src/policy.rs` precedent |
| **ephemeral event** | An event with `durability = ephemeral` (streaming deltas, permission *requests*, UI presentation facts): visible on `subscribe`, never returned by `read`, never hashed. | WS-B1 AC-B1-12 |
| **writer lease / lease generation** | The exclusive right to append to one run, held by one holder for a ttl; `lease_generation` strictly increases on every takeover and is the fencing token carried on every event; the ledger refuses stale generations (`Fenced`). | WS-B1 + WS-B2 §6.3 (same field); OpenHands `conversation_lease.py` precedent |
| **durable-before-visible** | The write-path invariant that an event becomes visible to views, streams, subagents and the reference monitor only after its append is durably acknowledged; readers stop at the last complete record. | Logos (provisional) + Codex/Pi/OpenHands precedent |
| **effect phase event** | One durable ledger event per WS-B2 effect-lifecycle state (`intended … abandoned`), all sharing one `effect_id`; exactly one terminal event closes each `effect_id`. | Co-owned WS-B1/WS-B2 |
| **content address** | `(hash_algorithm, digest, media_type, size)` computed over raw bytes with a blob domain tag; the identity of every artifact, snapshot, offloaded payload, configuration and context item the ledger references. | ADR-0029; WS-L4 owns naming/versioning over addresses |
| **payload offload** | Storing an event payload above the class threshold as a blob and referencing it by content address from `refs`; the event's hash covers the address, not the bytes, so redaction leaves the chain valid. | ADR-0029 |
| **lineage (`forked_from`)** | The chain of `(run_id, up_to_seq, head_hash)` references from a forked run back to its root; forks reference rather than copy; referenced prefixes are pinned against GC; bundle export materializes lineage. | ADR-0027 |
| **event class lowering** | The declared mapping from a native event class to the Hosting-ABI / ACP-style minimum observable vocabulary (`tool_call_update`, `state_update`, `usage_update`, …) used by surfaces and hosted-participant adapters; `none` where no external equivalent exists; carries `_meta`-style extension slots (T-LCD-11). | WS-B1 §6.3; WS-A4/J6 consume |
| **recovery decision** | The payload of `lifecycle.run.resumed{from_seq, lease, recovery_decision{last_durable_phase, action}}` recorded by WS-B3 when a run resumes; makes the resume choice auditable instead of implicit. | WS-B3 owns the decision procedure |
| **deterministic replay (capability)** | A declared capability of a control-strategy variant: control decisions are a pure function of the durable prefix with all nondeterminism confined to recorded events; tested by re-driving against recorded model I/O; `n/a` for variants that do not declare it. | ADR-0028; WS-F1 contract field |
| **event reconstruction** | Rebuilding any view or resuming a run from the durable prefix without re-executing committed effects or resampling the model; the Core durability guarantee. | ADR-0028 |
